topic: NASA's Roman Space Telescope held its aim to better than one hundred-thousandth of a degree in its first in-space pointing tests, and why its coronagraph needs that

through_line.name: the chunky silver space telescope
through_line.progression: the telescope launches, steadies itself, opens its wide eye, locks onto guide stars and finally hides a star to reveal a planet
through_line.resolution: the telescope returns to the opening view, holding its beam on the coin

blocks.vo_line: NASA's new Roman telescope barely moves at all. That's like keeping a laser on a dime from about one hundred fifty miles.
blocks.through_line_state: the telescope holds a thin beam dead still on a far-away coin
shots: CLOSE-UP, slow push-in: a thin bright beam lands on the small silver coin standing on a hilltop post and the coin flashes
WIDE, static: the beam stretches across rolling hills from the telescope hovering far away in the sky
EXTREME CLOSE-UP, static: the telescope's round barrel door swings open with a snap
LOW ANGLE MEDIUM, gentle drift: wind whips the grass around the post while the beam stays locked on the coin
HIGH ANGLE WIDE, static: the whole valley with the beam drawn straight from telescope to coin

blocks.vo_line: The Nancy Grace Roman Space Telescope launched this August, bound for a parking spot about one million miles from Earth.
blocks.through_line_state: the telescope rides the rocket up and pops free
shots: LOW ANGLE WIDE, static: the slim white rocket stands on the seaside pad with steam rolling out
CLOSE-UP, static: the engines ignite in a bright orange burst and the pad shakes
MEDIUM, crane up: the rocket climbs past the tower on a thick column of flame
EXTREME CLOSE-UP, static: the rocket's nose splits open with a pop and the telescope slides out
HIGH ANGLE WIDE, slow push-in: the telescope drifts away above the curved horizon as the sky darkens

blocks.vo_line: In September, engineers tested its aim. It stayed steady to within one hundred-thousandth of a degree for eight hours at a time.
blocks.through_line_state: the telescope wobbles, then locks rock steady on the coin target
shots: MEDIUM, gentle drift: the telescope floats among stars, wobbling slightly from side to side
EXTREME CLOSE-UP, static: small thrusters puff once and the wobble stops with a click
WIDE, static: a thin beam from the telescope reaches a tiny far-off coin and holds on it
CLOSE-UP, slow push-in: the coin glows steadily under the unmoving dot of light
OVERHEAD, static: the telescope sits perfectly still while the stars slowly wheel around it

blocks.vo_line: Roman's main mirror is the same width as Hubble's, yet each image covers at least one hundred times more sky.
blocks.through_line_state: the telescope opens wide and takes in a huge patch of sky
shots: CLOSE-UP, low angle: the telescope's barrel door lifts and the round mirror inside catches the light
WIDE, gentle drift: the telescope turns above the curved planet toward a field of stars
EXTREME CLOSE-UP, push-in: starlight sweeps across the mirror's surface
MEDIUM, static: a small square window of stars pops open in front of the telescope, then a far bigger one snaps open around it
HIGH ANGLE WIDE, static: the big window fills with a sea of stars with a soft chime

blocks.vo_line: Roman has no separate guider. Instead, eighteen detectors in its main camera each track a guide star, checking about four times every second.
blocks.through_line_state: the telescope's camera tiles each lock onto a star
shots: EXTREME CLOSE-UP, slow push-in: a grid of square tiles inside the telescope lights up one by one
MEDIUM, static: the telescope faces a cluster of bright stars along the planet's glowing edge
CLOSE-UP, gentle drift: a single star blinks rapidly inside one tile like a ticking light
WIDE, static: the telescope drifts a little, then nudges back into place with a soft thud
OVERHEAD, static: every tile holds its own star, all pulsing together

blocks.vo_line: Why so steady? Its coronagraph is designed to block a star's glare and reveal planets one hundred million times fainter.
blocks.through_line_state: the telescope slides a tiny disc over a blazing star and a planet appears
shots: WIDE, static: a blazing star floods the view, the telescope a small silhouette in front of it
CLOSE-UP, slow push-in: a small round disc slides out of the telescope and snaps over the star
EXTREME CLOSE-UP, static: the glare drops away and a tiny dot pops into view beside the disc
LOW ANGLE MEDIUM, gentle drift: the telescope holds still, the disc perfectly centered over the star
HIGH ANGLE WIDE, static: the little planet circles the hidden star, twinkling

blocks.vo_line: The coronagraph's first test captured stars in a neighboring galaxy, and NASA expects first images by early twenty twenty-seven. Which is wild, because
blocks.through_line_state: the telescope returns to holding its beam on the coin
shots: MEDIUM, slow push-in: a glowing swirl of stars rises over the hills at dusk
EXTREME CLOSE-UP, static: the telescope's barrel door opens with a clunk and light pours in
HIGH ANGLE WIDE, gentle drift: the telescope glides over the valley toward the hilltop post
LOW ANGLE CLOSE-UP, static: the coin on its post tilts up and catches a glint
WIDE, static: the thin beam lands on the coin again and holds, settling into the opening view
